analyst_view.overall: Early view: Forest under Oliver Glasner just beat Manchester City 3-1 by out-running them, with Liam Delap scoring twice, but they are 16th and were booed after losing to Brentford a week earlier. Brighton are second with the league's best attack (26 goals) and play Bournemouth three days before. It is Forest's press against Brighton's possession game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I agree: Brighton score a lot and Forest's attack has woken up with Delap, but Forest's games have been low-scoring all season (22 goals in 10) and Brighton concede very few. The two pull in opposite directions.

corners.text: The site has 9.8 corners. I lean higher: Brighton had almost 80% of the ball in the second half against Brentford, and teams pinned back by them concede corners. Forest will also win some from quick breaks down the wings.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean higher: Forest's press, led by Ryan Yates and Xaver Schlager, is built on hard duels in midfield, and stopping Brighton's passing often takes fouls. Five bookings looks more likely than four.

shots.text: The site has 26.8 shots. I agree: Brighton will take many shots and Forest will counter, so both sides should contribute. Nothing in the news moves this.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. I lean higher: Brighton have the best attack in the league, with Diego Gomez, Charalampos Kostoulas and Pascal Gross all scoring recently, and Delap is in form. More quality chances than the figure suggests.
